name: Commercial Bank of Dubai
founded: 1969 (incorporated in Dubai on 4 July 1969 by Emiri Decree; became a national public shareholding company in 1982)
ownership_summary: DFM-listed. At 31 Dec 2025 the Investment Corporation of Dubai (ICD) held 20% on behalf of the Government of Dubai; four other holders above 5% held 40.35%: Al Futtaim Private Co. LLC 17.46%, Orient Insurance PJSC 8.84%, Abdul Wahed Al Rostamani (AWR) Group 7.68% and Ghobash Trading & Investment Co. 6.37%; UAE nationals held 99.81% (AT1 prospectus 13 Jul 2026, S5; annual report 2025, S6; shareholder list updated Mar 2026, S10). Foreign ownership allowed up to 40% since Jun 2020.

shareholders.holder: Investment Corporation of Dubai (on behalf of the Government of Dubai)

government_link: Yes — 20% held by the Investment Corporation of Dubai on behalf of the Government of Dubai (as of 31 Dec 2025, S5). The prospectus states neither the Government nor ICD has a legal obligation to fund CBD. The Chairman and one other director were elected as ICD representatives (S6).
group_structure: Commercial Bank of Dubai PSC plus wholly owned subsidiaries: CBD Financial Services LLC (local shares and bonds brokerage), Attijari Properties LLC (property management), CBD Digital Lab Limited (technology and R&D for the parent; listed in the Jul 2026 prospectus), SPVs CBD (Cayman) Ltd, CBD (Cayman II) Ltd and VS 1897 (Cayman) Ltd with three BVI subsidiaries holding assets acquired in settlement of debt; associate National General Insurance Co. PJSC (17.8%). Islamic products are offered through the 'CBD Al Islami' window (since 18 Sep 2008), not a separate bank (S1, S5, S9). No separately profiled subsidiaries, so no double counting.

customer_segments: Institutional banking (large corporates, government, financial institutions), corporate banking (mid-sized and emerging corporates), personal banking (Essential, Elite, Private Banking tiers, plus business coverage and emerging corporate SME segments) and Islamic (CBD Al Islami) (S5, S14, S15).
business_lines: Four reported segments: Institutional Banking, Corporate Banking, Personal Banking and Trading & Other. Personal Banking produced AED 2,450m (41.4%) of FY2025 operating income and AED 1,249m (43%) of H1 2026 operating income (S2, S1, S5). Wealth: Elite and Private Banking with relationship managers and an Elite Management Centre / Private Banking Centre in Dubai; CBD Invest digital investing (US stocks/ETFs via Saxo Bank, launched Jul 2026); local brokerage through CBD Financial Services LLC; bancassurance; gold and silver accounts. Wholesale: trade finance, cash management, treasury, investment banking (syndications, DCM) (S5, S11, S16).

capabilities.wealth_summary: CBD runs wealth inside its Personal Banking Group (GM Retail & Business Banking: Dhiraj Kunwar, ex-RAKBANK, since Sep 2025) through two tiers: Elite (NRV AED 400k) and Private Banking (NRV AED 3.5m), served from Elite Management Centres and a Private Banking Centre in Dubai. On about 29–30 Jul 2026 it launched CBD Invest in the CBD Mobile App. CBD Invest offers execution-only trading in 7,000+ US-listed stocks and ETFs, with Saxo Bank as executing broker and possible custodian. It also has a 'Wealth 360' net-worth view that includes external assets, goal-based 'Spaces' and portfolio analytics. Fees are 0.25% per trade (min USD 3), and the bank says more asset classes are planned. Local DFM/ADX brokerage runs through the subsidiary CBD Financial Services LLC (est. 2005). The bank publishes no AUM; its FY2025 statements show only AED 11.8bn of fiduciary assets. The AT1 prospectus says the Board approved an operational plan to make CBD a leading financial services provider for HNWIs and affluent customers. No discretionary, structured-product, private-markets or Shariah investment offering was found.

segments.name: CBD Elite Banking
segments.eligibility: Net Relationship Value (investments + deposits + quarterly average CASA balance) of AED 400,000+, or monthly salary AED 50,000+ with NRV AED 200,000+; otherwise AED 175 + VAT monthly relationship fee

segments.name: CBD Private Banking
segments.eligibility: NRV AED 3,500,000+, or monthly salary AED 150,000+ with NRV AED 1,000,000+ (website); otherwise AED 350 + VAT monthly fee. The prospectus gives a different alternative (see discrepancies).

private_banking.detail: CBD Private Banking: a dedicated Private Relationship Manager, Private Banking lounges and 'comprehensive wealth management' covering preservation, growth and intergenerational legacy. Eligibility is NRV of AED 3.5m. Private Banking and Elite clients get CBD Invest plus RM and 'specialist investment expertise' support. The H1 2026 deck lists 2026 Digital Banker Global Private Banking Innovation awards (Best Private Bank Digital Innovation in Dubai; Most Innovative Business Model – Middle East). The current head of Private Banking is not named.

asset_management.detail: No asset-management subsidiary or CBD-branded fund range was found. The prospectus says Corporate Banking provides 'Syndication, Asset Management and Investment Advisory services'. The H1 2026 deck gives the treasury head's title as 'Head of Treasury, Asset Management & Global Markets'. CBD Invest is offered under CBD's 'Securities Portfolio Management' licence.

brokerage.detail: CBD Financial Services LLC (100%, est. 2005) provides brokerage for local shares and bonds on DFM and ADX through an online platform and mobile app, with margin trading. Its FAQ states there is no international market access. US-listed stocks and ETFs are offered separately through CBD Invest: CBD transmits orders and Saxo Bank acts as executing broker. CBD says it does not act as broker or dealer for these trades.

digital_investing.detail: CBD Invest launched in the CBD Mobile App around 29–30 Jul 2026 and is not available on internet banking. It offers 7,000+ US-listed stocks and ETFs through market, limit, stop and recurring buy orders, with no fractional shares. Other features: 'Wealth 360' net worth including manually added external assets and liabilities, goal 'Spaces', analytics benchmarked to the S&P 500 and NASDAQ, and a daily portfolio score. It is for UAE residents aged 21+ (not US nationals) with a CBD current or savings account, after CMA investor classification and appropriateness checks. Fees are 0.25% of trade value (min USD 3), with 0% commission promoted for new customers. It is execution-only with no advice. The legacy CBD Investr app page now redirects to CBD Invest.

advisory.detail: The launch release says Elite and Private Banking clients get dedicated relationship managers and 'specialist investment expertise' for portfolio construction and long-term planning. No advisory mandate or fee schedule was published. CBD Invest explicitly provides no advice.

discretionary.detail: No discretionary portfolio management offering found. The CBD Invest KFS states CBD does not provide discretionary portfolio management under that service.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No current model portfolios. A 2021 'CBD Investr' robo-advisory app is mentioned by WAM (seen in search results only). The CBD Investr web page now redirects to CBD Invest, which is self-directed.

funds_platform.detail: The website menu has a 'Mutual Funds' page, but it rendered blank on 2026-10-12, so the fund shelf and platform provider are unknown. CBD Invest offers ETFs only.

structured_products.detail: Not mentioned on the Private, Elite or CBD Invest pages, in the prospectus or in the annual report.

private_markets.detail: No private-markets or alternatives access found.

islamic_wealth.detail: CBD Al Islami, an Islamic window since 2008, offers Mudaraba savings, Wakala investment deposits and Ijara/Murabaha financing. No Shariah-compliant investment funds or portfolios were found.

partners.what: Named in the CBD Invest KFS and T&Cs as executing broker for international trades; 'may also provide custody and settlement services'
'Partnered with Udacity by Accenture to empower employees with skills in data and AI'; over 1,000 employees upskilled

initiatives.what: Press room lists MEED's 'MENA Best Digital Bank' (MENA Banking Excellence Awards 2026 – Retail, Digital & SME) and MEA Finance Banking Technology Awards 2026 recognitions.

Launched CBD Invest (digital wealth inside the CBD Mobile App) for affluent, Elite and Private Banking customers: US stocks/ETFs, Wealth 360 aggregation, goal-based investing and analytics; more asset classes planned. Trade press dated 29–30 Jul 2026.
Issued a USD 600m AT1 perpetual non-call-6 capital security.
Launched 'UP by CBD', a mobile bank for micro and small businesses.

Prospectus states the Board approved a separate operational plan aimed at making CBD a leading UAE financial services provider for HNWIs and affluent customers, with 'selective and measured growth' in Personal Banking.
Activated Open Finance at scale (first UAE bank, per CBD), completed ISO 20022 migration, launched Jaywan cards and moved to a dual-site Tier III private cloud.
Hired Dhiraj Kunwar from RAKBANK to lead Retail & Business Banking.

opportunities: CBD Invest is new (Jul 2026) and covers only US stocks and ETFs, execution-only. The bank says 'additional asset classes and enhanced capabilities will be introduced over time' (S18, S12).
No model portfolios, discretionary mandates, structured products, private markets or Shariah investment products were found for Elite or Private clients (S5, S11, S15).
The Board-approved plan targets leadership with HNWIs and affluent customers. Personal Banking contributed 41.4% of FY2025 operating income (S5).
Elite and Private tiers are defined by NRV that includes investment value (S14, S15). Fiduciary assets were AED 11.8bn at 31 Dec 2025 (S2).
The CEO holds a PhD in Artificial Intelligence, and the bank publicises AI upskilling of 1,000+ staff and 2026 private-banking digital innovation awards (S5, S4).
barriers: Saxo Bank is already the executing broker and possible custodian behind CBD Invest (S12, S13).
The builder of the CBD Invest app is not disclosed. CBD has an in-house technology subsidiary (CBD Digital Lab Limited) and a 'Default Digital' programme (S5).
The strategy prioritises wholesale banking. Personal Banking growth is described as 'selective and measured' (S5).
Leadership churn in 2025–2026: new heads of retail (Sep 2025), wholesale (Oct 2025), risk (Apr 2026) and customer, and the COO's status is unclear (S5, S6, S7).
incumbent_vendors: Saxo Bank: execution, custody and settlement for CBD Invest US stocks/ETFs (S12, S13)
